summary: The E07 is a large five-seat electric SUV whose glass rear dome and tailgate open to turn the load area into a short ute-style bay, sold as a 252kW RWD or a 440kW AWD Performance on a 90kWh battery. Australian reviewers agree it is plush, roomy and well equipped, and CarExpert named it its 2026 Best Large EV SUV, but they split on whether the transforming body earns its complexity: CarsGuide (6.8/10) and Chasing Cars (6.5/10) both say it is no substitute for a real ute and drives without much engagement. Sales were paused in March 2026 and 218 early cars recalled to add a missing centre-rear child-seat tether, since fitted, and Deepal's Australian distribution passes from Inchcape to Changan by April 2027.
pros: Long range for the class: 550km WLTP for the RWD and 510km for the AWD Performance from a 90kWh battery, with reviewers seeing 15-18kWh/100km in real driving
Fast 240kW peak DC charging (30-80% in about 15 minutes, claimed) and 6.6kW vehicle-to-load
Practical layout no rival matches: 524L boot growing to 1,654L, a 131L drainable frunk, an open-air load bay with the dome retracted, and 1,500kg braked towing
Comfortable air-suspended ride, spacious flat-floored rear seat with heating, ventilation and massage, and a long equipment list from the $64,900 RWD
7-year/160,000km vehicle warranty and 8-year/240,000km battery warranty, with capped-price servicing of about $2,950 (RWD) over seven years
cons: Not a ute: the fastback roof limits tall loads, the bay's dynamic payload is only 300kg, and Deepal quotes no GCM, so it will not replace a dual-cab for trade work
Unengaging and loose-handling: light steering, soft body control, jerky low-speed throttle on the AWD Performance and a 12.3m turning circle
Many motorised parts and an overloaded touchscreen with no conventional instrument cluster or glovebox, which reviewers flag as long-term reliability and distraction risks
Small, newly restructured brand: the early-2026 stop-sale and recall, a distributor change to Changan, no ANCAP rating and no resale history make depreciation hard to predict
